text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Private cluster 'acme-prod-vpc-1' GPU queue growth >90% over 5m. Autoscaler failing to provision nodes (scale_retries=3). Link: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/1950012345
maria.g: paging @ops-shift and @samir — customer-impacting, ACME is seeing timeouts on batch infer.
ops-shift: I'm on it. Checking cluster logs in eu-west1-onprem-az1.
samir: initial glance — kube events show pods stuck Pending due to "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" and node bootstrap timeouts. Not seeing new nodes in nodepool for last 8m.
samir: kubectl get pods -n acme | grep Pending

```
acme-infer-0 Pending 0/1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
acme-infer-1 Pending 0/1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
acme-batcher-0 Pending 0/2 ImagePullBackOff
```

lee: any rate limit on node creation from customer's onprem? last I saw the customer's vSphere was throttling API calls.
ops-shift: vSphere API shows many 429s. Controller tries to create VM, but provisioning queue > 60s. autoscaler backoff hit max retries.
eva: ACME has reserved capacity set to 4 GPUs but current queue needs ~12 GPUs (peak). Autoscaler cap was set to 6 for cost limits.
kyle: possible quick mitigation — temporarily raise autoscaler cap to 12 and enable parallel bootstrap=4. We can also enable a temporary re-route to Redwood Dedicated for ACME to avoid errors.
maria.g: customer ask — are we able to failover them to Dedicated? legal-wise ok for this customer (contracted fallback).
ops-shift: starting manual override: set autoscaler.max=12 and parallel_bootstrap=4. Command:

```
redwood infra autoscaler update --cluster acme-prod-vpc-1 --max-nodes 12 --parallel-bootstrap 4
```

deploy-bot: autoscaler config update accepted (change-id: cfg-99231). Applying... 
ops-shift: triggering manual node creations for 6 nodes to speed up. Command:

```
redwood infra node create --cluster acme-prod-vpc-1 --count 6 --type gpu-p4
```

samir: seeing node creation started, vSphere tasks in progress. ETA ~6m per node.
lee: I'm notifying infra-eng (cc @kyle) to watch vsphere API quiesce.
kyle: enabling dedicated fallback for acme (temp) and moving 30% traffic:

```
redwood route update --customer acme --fallback dedicated --weight 30
```

eva: customer-facing update: "We're seeing elevated latency and some timeouts for inference; working on provisioning more GPU capacity. Temporary routing to Dedicated started. ETA to stable ~15-20m." Sent message to acme-support@acme.com
maria.g: monitoring: queue length peaked at 18k tokens/min, error rate 7%, median latency for text-gen 5.2s -> 9.1s tail.
ops-shift: first 3 nodes came online. Pod scheduling started, KV cache warm-up in progress.
samir: rebalancer is draining some rooted pods — expect transient 502s as replicas spin up.
ops-shift: after nodes up, queue dropped to 30% of peak and errors down to 1.5%.
lee: root cause: customer's vSphere API rate-limited node creation and our autoscaler had a cost cap too low for this customer's sudden spike. Need runbook updates: - detect vSphere 429s as 'bootstrapping bottleneck' alert - auto-increase parallel_bootstrap when queue > X and customer fallback allowed - add automatic dedicated-fallback toggle for contract-eligible customers.
kyle: opening follow-up ticket and scheduling oncall/infra postmortem. I'll include timeline and config diffs.
maria.g: good. Oncall handoff to @ops-shift in 20m for wrap and follow-ups.
ops-shift: leaving note: manual nodes created + routing fallback, customer stable. continuing monitoring. :white_check_mark:
